summary: All three round 1 findings resolved correctly. The new test_cas_status_preserves_unknown_lines is particularly strong — it exercises the implementation fix at the I/O level (asserts raw file contents) and then verifies load() still surfaces only valid jobs. No new findings. 34 tests, all clean.

F1_caplog_count_assertion.notes: test_load_skips_blank_and_malformed_lines now builds warning_records list and asserts len == 1 with an explanatory error message. The rationale (blank/whitespace lines are silent skips, not errors) is documented inline. This is the right call — counting only the bad-JSON warning and not the blank-line noise is precise.

F2_illegal_transition_file_immutability.notes: test_cas_status_raises_on_illegal_transition now reads pre = tmp_queue_path.read_bytes() before the raises block and asserts equality after. The implementation raises IllegalTransitionError before acquiring the lock (static graph check), so no I/O can occur — the test is now pinning that ordering as a correctness guarantee.

F3_conftest_placeholder_shapes.notes: All three placeholder fixtures (mock_blogger_run_campaign_from_article, mock_mnemonic_mcp_stdio, mock_claude_subprocess) now have detailed docstrings describing the return shape Task 6 will configure. The mock_claude_subprocess already had returncode=0 set; the docstring now explains the communicate() tuple contract too. This is exactly what Task 6 needs.

test_cas_status_preserves_unknown_lines.notes: The test exercises a real data-loss scenario: a half-written line (no closing brace, no newline) is appended after a valid job, then cas_status is called on the valid job. After the CAS the test asserts (a) the raw truncated string is still present in the file, and (b) load() still returns exactly the one valid job. This validates both the implementation behavior and the user-facing contract. The truncated line chosen (no closing brace) is a realistic kill-9 artifact. No litmus-test failure — deleting the preservation logic in cas_status would cause this test to fail.

pyramid_assessment.note: Still all unit, appropriate for Task 4 scope.
